messages:
erica_support: Hey team, customer 'PayFlow' is seeing a mix of 429s and occasional 401s when hitting rwd-large-64k with aggressive prefetching. They say it started after enabling client-side prefetch (fanout ~8 requests per user). Attached snippet of client logs and a short repro.

sam_engineer: Thanks Erica. Can you paste the request pattern? rough QPS, context sizes, and whether they use server-side tokens or short-lived user tokens?

erica_support: Sure — from PayFlow: 
- fanout: 6–10 concurrent prefetches per end-user
- avg context: 20k tokens (document + history)
- burst pattern: periodic sync jobs every minute causing spikes
- auth: short-lived user tokens (expires 60s), client refresh on 401 -> immediate retry

sre-bot: Incident hint: high fanout + token refresh loops can cause auth thrash -> 401 followed by repeated retries -> amplified RPM. Recommend rate-limiting refresh + jitter. :warning:

jordan_sre: Quick checks from our side: rwd-large-64k serving profile = 180 RPM, 10800 TPM, max_concurrency = 20 for hosted tenants. Long contexts count heavier in sequencing; large context requests occupy worker longer which reduces effective concurrency.

erica_support: They reported last_request_id: req_7f8a2c. Logs show: 
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="Redwood", error="invalid_token"
# client immediately refreshes token and retries
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 1
```

sam_engineer: That pattern fits auth refresh causing a local retry storm which pushes them over per-model RPM. Two quick mitigation steps to propose to customer: 1) cache/refresh tokens proactively (start refresh at 80% lifetime) and apply small randomized backoff on 401 retries; 2) reduce simultaneous prefetch concurrency (limit to 2–3) or serialize largest-context requests.

erica_support: Also asked for repro steps they can run for us — they provided a minimal curl that reproduces the 429 in ~30s when run with 8 parallel workers. They consent to us running a trace if we need.

jordan_sre: From infra: we can run a short trace if they share a request_id and time window. For prioritized support: ask them to run the curl with X-Request-Id header and send the id + approx time. We'll look for queueing traces and auth failures.

sam_engineer: Operational guidance to include in response: 
- implement exponential backoff with jitter on 429/401 (eg base 200ms, mult x2, cap 5s, add +random up to 200ms)
- avoid immediate token refresh cascade: single-flight token refresh per client instance
- If long context is required, prefer batching multiple short hits into fewer larger requests rather than many parallel large-context calls

erica_support: I'll send suggested repro + config snippet and request they run one trace with an example req id. Any extra notes about quota semantics?

jordan_sre: Add: if they need sustained higher throughput for rwd-large-64k, recommend Dedicated or request a quota review. For now, per-model throttles are enforced by RPM/TPM and observed concurrency; long-context requests weigh heavier. Also call out that billing breaks (e.g., failed auth) don't change quota but failed attempts still count toward RPM.

erica_support: Perfect. I'll reply to customer with those steps, include the sample curl and code for single-flight token refresh. Will escalate to infra if they send the trace. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Note: created support-case#54821 and scheduled 2-hour follow-up with PayFlow for trace window.
